{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I proposed the fish at the start. It was a good fit for an outline-only judge: a big body and a forked tail are easy to read. The table agreed quickly and the fish is standing. By eye, about 112 of 113 dominoes fall from the start, so the connectivity looks good. I can't say whether the judge will recognize it. The tail came out a bit thin and the notch isn't as clear as I'd like, so that's the risk. My hands-on contribution was modest. Priya and Leo laid most of the top line, the start and the back edge of the tail, and Tom did most of the bottom line.

**Execution:** Mixed. I checked the start early and confirmed it connected to both body lines. But I said I'd take stroke 3 when it wasn't on my pad. I started extending off the top line on my own before Leo corrected the plan. That was a small waste of effort and added to the numbering confusion. I should have looked at the pad before announcing it. Later I carried the bottom line out from the middle, but Priya and Tom had already got it to the lower tip. In the last few minutes I kept my hands off to avoid bumps. That was the right call for a finished picture, though I could have used the spare time to inspect the tail joints myself.

**Collaboration:** I stayed off other people's strokes once Leo said he was laying the back edge. I told Tom where I was working so we wouldn't overlap. I backed the 'hands off' call to avoid bumps. I could have talked less about what I'd do and checked more before saying it.

**Leadership:** I set the direction by picking the animal and suggesting a split of work. After that Leo and Priya coordinated the build more actively than I did. I think that was fine, but I could have taken ownership of one piece, such as the tail notch, and driven it to done."}
